verificationScope: Explorer verification of the deployment-era bytecode, not parity with this current public source tree. Measured 2026-08-21: 3 of 13 checked deployments passed the strict length-and-metadata gate (all three mocks); eight protocol contracts had equal length but different metadata, while LenderPool and ReferralRegistry differed in size. The later referral-only source correction leaves that result at 3 of 13 because the live ReferralRegistry still differs.
note: Mock DexFi stack. Real DexFi bonds exist only on Base mainnet, so MockUSDC/MockBond/MockFarm stand in and mirror the verified ABIs including the whitelist gate. The adapter is self-whitelisted here; on mainnet that is DexFi's call and the current integration requirement.

lockState.status: OPEN - PRE-LOCKDOWN BYTECODE. NOT A GAP IN THE RECORD, A STATEMENT ABOUT THE CHAIN.
lockState.note: Every null here is a positive statement rather than an unknown, in the same sense as libraries.CreditWiring.address below. admin(), operator() and lockAuthority() REVERT on all three addresses above, because the deployed bytecode PREDATES the MockLockdown gate entirely. Measured 2026-08-30 by cast against Base Sepolia, and again by the entrypoint named in verifiedBy, which exits non-zero with PreLockdownBytecode. The deployed runtime sizes are 2385 / 5594 / 3136 against a tree at 2945 / 7657 / 4509, so the live stack is an older and strictly smaller generation. The practical consequence is that the mock CONFIGURATION surface on this deployment is open to any caller: setBlocked, setRewardPool, setWhitelisted, setPendingYield and setRevertOnWithdraw were all executed successfully from a role-less address. Worth naming specifically: setPendingYield forges the delivered-farm-yield counter, which is the counter the four-clean-epoch evidence is measured on.
lockState.whyThisRowExists: The source in this repository added a lockdown gate to the mock stack and wired it into the deploy script. That mitigation is TREE-ONLY. It is not on the deployed contracts, and nothing on chain, in CI or in the off-chain jobs said so. This row says it, in the file a reader checks first, and it needed no redeploy to be true.
lockState.publicRecordCaveat: This public record deliberately omits `deployer` and `operators` - see operatorsNote above, and read them from the contracts if you want them. The AssertLocked entrypoint resolves both from the deployment record, so run against a record that carries them, or pass RECOUP_KEEPER and compare the deployer against the chain by hand. That is a property of what this file publishes, not a defect in the script.

CreditWiring.status: LINKED BY THE TREE, NEVER DEPLOYED. A null address is a positive statement, not a gap: this library did not exist when the 2026-08-19 set was deployed, so there is nothing at this set for CreditManager to have been linked against. The bytecode gate reads this block, and a null here makes the CreditManager link a REPORTED condition instead of a hard failure - but only while CreditManager's own runtime length still diverges from the tree's. If it ever matches while this is null, the gate FAILS, because a CreditManager that is byte-compatible with a tree linking a library that does not exist is a contradiction in the record rather than drift.
CreditWiring.onTheNextRedeploy: forge script deploys an unlinked library automatically, as a CREATE2 through the deterministic deployer at 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C ahead of the contract that links it - so its address depends on the creation code and a zero salt rather than on a nonce, and is predictable before the broadcast. MEASURED on a disposable fork on 2026-08-26: the run emits 44 transactions against the 2026-08-19 run's 40, one of which is this library and three of which are the setGuardian calls that did not exist then. Copy the library's address in here, replacing the null, in the same edit that updates contracts. The gate then reads its runtime code like any other row and additionally verifies solc's call-protection word - the PUSH20 of the library's own address that its constructor patches in - against this address, which is the library confirming its own identity.
CreditWiring.why: CreditManager delegatecalls it, and its artifact carries six link offsets (2738, 8155, 14770, 14935, 19888, 20034 - read out of linkReferences, not counted by hand). The split was forced by EIP-170: the manager measured 24,512 bytes against a 24,576 limit before the move, and measures 22,079 on a clean build of this tree as of 2026-09-01. That last figure is a dated snapshot rather than a standing fact - it read 22,015 until the guardian pair landed - so re-measure with forge build --sizes rather than quoting it from here.

referralRegistryNote: Carried over from the 2026-08-03 deployment. Its 1489-byte runtime predates the NON_BINDABLE tombstone guard and still exposes delegated registerFor; measured on 2026-08-20, registerFor(code, NON_BINDABLE) from a stranger succeeded. Current source fixes the broader design by deleting registerFor and requiring partner self-registration, but the registry is unused, holds no value and is not read by the protocol. The committed address remains defective; do not use it for referrals. Live replacement is disabled and unauthorised.

One local deployment transaction used 841101 gas and emitted 16 CodeRegistered reservation logs. riskParameters.sourceOfTruth: the chain, read from RiskParams at 0xb2592dc47250b2546273a64c3736bc4c01cea49e
riskParameters.closedNote: The divergence recorded here from 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-19 is CLOSED. These four values were read back from RiskParams on chain after the redeploy and match Config.sol's declared defaults exactly. They are storage now, not bytecode constants, so a governance retune moves them without a redeploy and this record has to be updated when that happens.

operatorsNote: Owner, yield recipient, keeper and NAV confirmer are four distinct addresses, and every protocol contract was verified on-chain as owned by the configured owner rather than by the deployer. Read them from the contracts if you want them. The testnet operator keys are throwaways funded from a faucet; a mainnet deployment does not reuse that pattern.

state.liquiditySourceFundedNote: 250,000 mUSDC. That is TEN TIMES the current DEFAULT_GLOBAL_BORROW_CAP of 25,000e6, which is fine because over-funding a testnet float refuses nothing. Deliberately not described as equal to the cap: that claim was in this file and wrong by ten times for nine days.
state.navBootstrapNote: Bootstrapped 2026-08-19T12:33:24Z at 2182440000, i.e. $21.8244, which is the keeper's own independently computed figure and NOT DexFi's displayed $24.81. Seeding at theirs would have put the keeper's first post about 12% out and parked it for the confirmer on day one, which is the same reasoning the 2026-08-03 deploy used. bootstrapNav is onlyOwner and the owner is not the deploying address, so it was a separate step. It is one-shot and reverts AlreadyBootstrapped, so it cannot be corrected without redeploying the oracle and repointing everything at it.

seededPosition.sizingNote: Sized against the parameters agreed with DexFi on 2026-08-07 and enforced on chain since the 2026-08-19 redeploy. 1000 bonds at $21.8244 is $21,824.40 of collateral; the 2500 bps ceiling allows $5,456.10 and perAccountBorrowCap cuts that to $5,000. $4,000 lands at 1832 bps. The old deployment's 6,000 USDC position at 2772 bps is not reachable under these parameters.
seededPosition.disbursementNote: borrow(4000000000) booked 4,000,000,000 of debt and disbursed 3,975,000,000, with 25 USDC topping up the prepaid liquidation bounty escrow. bountyEscrowOf now returns 25000000 rather than reverting, which it did on the 2026-08-03 bytecode, so the webapp's three-state escrow sentinel has two reachable states on this deployment rather than three.
seededPosition.parametersAreBindingNote: Readback is not the same as enforcement, so both were checked. healthFactor 2.729 equals collateral x 0.50 / debt, which is the 5000 bps threshold and not the old 5800 (that would give 3.165). And borrow(1100000000) on top reverts PerAccountCapExceeded with 5,100,000,000 requested against a 5,000,000,000 cap.

previousDeployments.note: Replaced by the 2026-08-19 redeploy, which closed the risk-parameter divergence. Those contracts are still on chain and still hold the old seeded position, but nothing points at them. They enforce MAX_LTV 3500 / threshold 5800 / global cap 250,000 / per-account 25,000 in bytecode and have no RiskParams, which is why they could not be retuned.
previousDeployments.schemaNote: THIS IS A LIST, NEWEST FIRST, and it used to be a single previousDeployment object. That single slot held exactly one superseded set, so the next redeploy would have displaced this 2026-08-03 entry along with its note - a lossy edit that reads like a move, because the keys stay and the diff does not look like a deletion. This is the third generation, so one slot had been outgrown twice. Adding a generation now means prepending an object here and nothing else.
